examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression Using the Secant-Tangent Identity: Replacing a Squared Secant
examples.problem: Express $(1-\sec x )(1+\sec x )$ in terms of $\tan x$ only.
examples.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the secant-tangent identity:

$$
1+\tan^2 x = \sec^2{x}
$$

First, we expand the parentheses using the difference of squares formula:

$$
(1-\sec x )(1+\sec x ) = 1 - \sec^2x
$$

Then, we rewrite the expression using the secant-tangent identity as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-{sec}^{2}⁡x & =1-(1+{tan}^{2}⁡x) \\  & =1-1-{tan}^{2}⁡x \\  & =-{tan}^{2}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
(1-\sec x )(1+\sec x )= -\tan^2 x.
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the secant-tangent identity:

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta 
$$

We rewrite the given expression using the secant-tangent identity as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta +{tan}^{3}⁡\theta }{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta } & =\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \text{ }\,(1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta )}{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \,{sec}^{2}⁡\theta }{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \cancel{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta }}{\cancel{{sec}^{2}⁡\theta }} \\  & =\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta +{tan}^{3}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta \operatorname{sec}⁡\theta }=\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta .
$$
